title: Leadership team diagnostic: 72 questions, 21 scales, 3 outcomes
description: Every member answers 72 statements across 21 scales and 3 outcomes, anonymously. The results show level, agreement and one standing per scale.
kicker: Available now · part of the Team plan
lead: The fuller look, once the scan has shown what to talk about. Every member answers 72 statements, one per screen and in mixed order, across 21 scales and 3 outcomes. Answers carry a random ID, never a name. When the round closes, everyone sees the same results, scale by scale.
summary: 72 statements across 21 scales and 3 outcomes, with results in three depths.

items.title: Say what you see, safely
points: Each statement is about the team, never about a colleague.
Stored with a random ID, never with your name.
Progress is saved on your device until you submit.

items.title: The whole picture, scale by scale
points: Conditions, processes and states, and the outcomes they lead to.
Everyone is asked, and nobody is picked out.
A count while it runs, never a score or a name.

items.title: A measure you can repeat
points: The same published statements in every round.
Built on the research on leadership teams, and labelled research-based, not yet validated.
No result below the anonymity threshold.

blocks.title: The leader opens a round
blocks.text: The leader opens the Full diagnostic, and every current member is asked. There is no picker for who takes part. The round stays open for 14 days.
points: One round answers at a time.
A group needs at least as many members as its threshold, 4 or more.
blocks.alt: Assess: round 2 of the Full diagnostic, answering, with “5 of 8 answered. Counts only, never names.” and “You answered”.
blocks.caption: Round 1, answering: 5 of 8.

blocks.title: Before the first question
blocks.text: Each member sees what the round asks and how answers are kept: with a random ID, never with a name. Results open to everyone when the round closes.
blocks.alt: The Full diagnostic’s intro: 72 statements, one per screen, in mixed order, and how the answers are kept.
blocks.caption: What a member sees before they start.

blocks.title: One statement per screen
blocks.text: 72 statements in one mixed order, never grouped by scale. A member can skip and come back, and a review lists the gaps before “Submit anonymously”.
points: Progress is kept on the device until submit.
The same order for every member of the round.
blocks.alt: A statement on a phone: 1 of 72, “Our units work towards the same goals.”, with Agree chosen.
blocks.caption: The first of 72 statements, on a phone.

blocks.title: Results, for everyone at once
blocks.text: When the round is released, every member sees the same results at the same moment. The three outcomes come first, then the 21 scales by layer.
points: Each scale shows its level, an agreement label and one standing.
Each carries its evidence rating, from strong to not yet rated.
Change shows only between two rounds, and only when it is large enough to mean something.
blocks.alt: Results for round 1: the three outcomes, then the six conditions, each with evidence, level, change, agreement and standing.
blocks.caption: The overview of a released round.

blocks.title: A scale, explained
blocks.text: Each scale opens on a page of its own: what it means, its level, agreement and standing, its guidance and its evidence. One step further shows each question’s mean.
points: Guidance is worded as firmly as the scale’s evidence allows.
Never a lowest or highest score, a distribution, or one person’s answer.
blocks.alt: The scale Meeting goals: level 3.5, views differ, first round, with what it suggests and the evidence behind it, rated moderate.
blocks.caption: One scale, one level deeper.

blocks.text: A round, from open to result

items.title: Answering
items.text: Every member is asked. The page shows a count, never a score.

items.title: Closed
items.text: On its date, or when everyone has answered. Scores are computed once.

items.title: Released
items.text: With at least 4 answers, every member sees the result at the same moment.

blocks.title: Below the threshold
blocks.text: A round with fewer answers than the threshold gets one extension of seven days. If there are still too few, no result is made and the answers are deleted.

items.title: 72 statements
items.text: One per screen, about the team as a whole.

items.title: 21 scales
items.text: Conditions, processes and states, each with its evidence rating.

items.title: 3 outcomes
items.text: Direction, alignment and commitment; viability; and member growth.

blocks.text: The [research page](/research) lists every scale, how it is read and how strong its evidence is.

blocks.title: In development
blocks.text: Reminder emails to those who have not answered are being set up. A reminder never says who else has or has not answered.

faq.q: Can the leader see who has answered?
faq.a: No. Everyone sees the count, such as 5 of 8 answered. Each person sees only whether they have answered themselves.
For each scale, its level, an agreement label and one standing, with its evidence rating. Never a lowest or highest score, a distribution or anyone’s answers.
Their progress is saved on their device until they submit, for as long as the round is open.

faq.q: What if fewer than four answer?
faq.a: The round gets one extension of seven days. If there are still too few answers, no result is made and the answers are deleted.

faq.q: How does a group get it?
faq.a: The Full diagnostic is part of the Team plan. A group’s leader can start a 14-day trial in the app, with no billing details.
